quarterly_data.signal: IREN's 10-K names NVIDIA among the limited number of suppliers from which it sources GPUs, networking and storage equipment for its AI Cloud Services; GPUs installed and on order as of June 30, 2026 included NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, B300, GB300 and VR200 systems. The 10-K states that demand for NVIDIA GPUs and certain networking equipment far exceeds supply, and that delivery delays due to industry-wide component shortages, principally relating to NVIDIA equipment, previously delayed certain equipment required for delivery of Horizon 1 under the Microsoft Agreement.
IREN's 10-K also names Lenovo and Gigabyte among the limited number of suppliers from which it sources hardware such as GPUs, networking and storage equipment for its AI Cloud Services.

IREN's 10-K reports commitments of $13,810.0 million as of June 30, 2026, versus $368.8 million as of June 30, 2025; these commitments include committed capital expenditure on AI hardware and infrastructure related to site development. The increase was primarily due to commitments related to its expansion into AI Cloud Services, including committed capital expenditure on computer hardware and infrastructure for site development of Horizons 1-4 at the Childress site, the Sweetwater 1 and Sweetwater 2 sites and the transition of the Childress and British Columbia data centers to AI Cloud. The figure does not reflect hardware purchase agreements and other contracts entered into after June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: commitments $13,810.0 million at June 30, 2026 (vs $368.8 million at June 30, 2025)
